subject: Inference constraints & qualification — latency/concurrency targets (Novus AI)
summary: Post-call recap summarizing latency and concurrency pain points, success criteria for PoC, and concrete next steps (trial access, eng deep-dive, MAP).
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@novusai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Inference constraints & qualification — latency/concurrency targets (Novus AI)

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from my side so we have a shared starting point and can move the PoC forward.

Key pain points you described:
- End users notice stutter on streaming responses in the web UI at higher concurrency (20–40 concurrent users per shard).
- Spiky traffic (short bursts) causes token-level latency to jump; affects demoability.
- Existing stack (on-prem Triton + internal batching) is hard to scale for mixed short/long prompts.

Current stack and constraints you mentioned:
- Model: a 13B open model served via internal Triton endpoints (quantized).
- Avg request: 60 tokens; ~1.2 tokens/sec generation pacing (user token-by-token UX).
- Target P95 per-token latency target: around 150–250ms (you indicated 200ms as a practical goal).
- Throughput target: sustained 2k tokens/sec with burst to 6k tokens/sec across the cluster.

Success criteria for a PoC (what you told us):
1) Streaming UX: first token appearance < 150ms after request start for low-latency flows.
2) P95 per-token <= 250ms at baseline concurrency.
3) No regression in output quality compared to your current quantized Triton runs.
4) Clear unit-cost estimate for production (tokens/sec cost + infra guidance).

What we recommend as immediate next steps:
- Redwood provides trial keys + sandbox endpoint for Novus to run a 2-week PoC.
- Share a small representative request log (anonymized) so our infra team can tune batching / cache sizing.
- Marcus to do a tech deep-dive next week (30–45m) to validate KV/caching options and initial capacity plan.
- We’ll send an initial SLA/proposal PDF and a short MAP (mutual action plan) within 24 hours.

Attachments: [attachment: initial-sla-proposal.pdf (PDF, 48KB)], [attachment: redwood-trial-setup.md (MD, 3KB)]

Proposed times for deep-dive: Tue 12/1 or Wed 12/2, 10–12 PST. Which works for you?

Thanks — look forward to moving quickly.

— Priyom
Priyom Das | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@novusai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novusai.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Inference constraints & qualification — latency/concurrency targets (Novus AI)

Thanks, Priyom — this is a helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side before Marcus digs in: 

Quoted for context: 
> Key pain points you described:
> - End users notice stutter on streaming responses in the web UI at higher concurrency (20–40 concurrent users per shard).

Clarifications / notes:
- The 20–40 concurrent users number is per application shard; overall traffic is spread across 6 shards in prod. We see bursts during business hours where a shard gets as many as 70 concurrent streams for 30–90s.
- When we say "first token <150ms" we mean time-to-first-byte for the streaming API (user-perceived latency), not just kernel-level per-token execution. So networking + gateway layer counts.
- We can deliver anonymized logs; procurement/ops will package the sample and send via secure link. Daniel (cc’d) will coordinate procurement and any IP/security forms.

One more ask for your PoC proposal: can you include a fallback plan for degraded capacity (e.g., fall back to a smaller model with consistent streaming UX) and a simple roll-back procedure? That’s going to be a major assessment criterion for our platform team.

We’re available for the deep-dive on Wed 12/2 at 11:00 PST.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez | Head of Platform, Novus AI
alicia@novusai.com | +1 (650) 555-6640

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@novusai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Inference constraints & qualification — latency/concurrency targets (Novus AI)

Looping in some quick technical notes before the Wed deep-dive. I want to make sure we set expectations for the PoC so the trial data is actionable.

1) What we’ll measure during the trial:
- Time-to-first-byte at the edge (includes network/gateway) and per-token compute latency.
- Token-level P50/P95/P99 across request-size buckets (<=32 tokens, 33–128, >128).
- Throughput and batch-utilization metrics.

2) Preliminary capacity guidance (subject to request distribution):
- For your stated workload (avg 60 tokens, burst to 6k tps) we’d start PoC with: 4 x A100-class GPUs behind our serving runtime with aggressive KV caching enabled.
- If low latency is the priority (first-token <150ms), we’ll prioritize smaller batch windows, prefix cache warmup, and keep a hot-standby small-model variant for fallback.

3) Data we need from Novus before the deep-dive:
- Representative anonymized request log (timestamps, token counts, streaming vs non-streaming) — 24–72 hours of traces preferred.
- Any gateway/proxy timeouts or client-side retry rules (these affect observed UX).

4) Fallback options we can offer in the MAP:
- Model variant routing: serve smaller quantized model for latency-sensitive requests; route long-context or quality-critical flows to the full model.
- Auto-fallback: if queueing exceeds threshold, route to reserved capacity or degrade to truncated responses.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for the Wed call and an example Kibana dashboard template we can send ahead.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Inference constraints & qualification — latency/concurrency targets (Novus AI)

Perfect — thanks Alicia and Marcus. Quick checklist / agreed next steps so they’re explicit: 

Action items:
- Novus (Daniel): share anonymized request logs and procurement contact info via the secure link (Daniel to send by EOD Tue 11/30).
- Redwood (Marcus): deliver runbook + dashboard template and initial capacity estimate (by Tue EOD 12/1).
- Redwood (Priyom): send trial credentials and MAP doc; include fallback options and SLA draft (sent now: link + attachment).
- Schedule: Deep-dive Wed 12/2 11:00 PST (calendar invite to follow).

Attachments / links included: [attachment: initial-sla-proposal.pdf], [attachment: redwood-trial-setup.md], MAP (live): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcMAP-example

If anything changes to the schedule, let me know. We’ll aim to keep the PoC turnkey and minimize required ops work on your side.

Thanks — excited to get started.

— Priyom
